title: The Sacred Household
subtitle: William Gouge — Domestical Duties
description: Begin a new month exploring the Puritan vision of the Christian home with William Gouge's masterwork 'Of Domesticall Duties.' Discover why the Puritans called the family a little church and how mutual submission in the fear of God transforms every household relationship.
memoryVerse: Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. -- Ephesians 5:21
discussionQuestions: What does it mean to call the family 'a little church'? In what ways does our family already function like a church?
Paul tells husbands to love their wives 'as Christ loved the church.' What are some practical ways this self-sacrificing love can be shown?
How does the fear of God change the way family members treat each other?

title: The Husband's Sacred Charge
subtitle: William Gouge — Domestical Duties
description: William Gouge outlines the husband's duties of sacrificial love, faithful provision, and respectful partnership, showing how a husband's treatment of his wife either preaches the true gospel or a false one.
memoryVerse: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it. -- Ephesians 5:25
discussionQuestions: Gouge says a harsh husband 'preaches a false gospel' to his wife. What does he mean by this?
What is the difference between 'nourishing' and 'cherishing'? Why does a wife need both?
How can a husband provide spiritual leadership in practical, daily ways?

title: The Wife's Noble Calling
subtitle: William Gouge — Domestical Duties
description: Explore the dignity and nobility of the wife's calling in the Puritan household — from the Proverbs 31 woman's industry and wisdom to the mother's irreplaceable role in nurturing children in the faith.
memoryVerse: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come. -- Proverbs 31:25
discussionQuestions: What does strength look like in everyday life? How is it different from the world's idea of strength?
Gouge calls the wife her husband's 'yoke-fellow.' What does this word picture suggest about marriage?
Why does Gouge consider the mother's role in educating children so important?

title: Training Up a Child
subtitle: William Gouge — Domestical Duties
description: Gouge addresses the most urgent parental duty — bringing children to the knowledge of God through diligent instruction, loving discipline, and fervent daily prayer for their souls.
memoryVerse: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it. -- Proverbs 22:6
discussionQuestions: What are some natural moments in our daily routine where we can talk about God together?
Why is it important for children to understand the reason behind correction?
Why is prayer even more important than instruction or discipline?

title: Honor Thy Father and Mother
subtitle: William Gouge — Domestical Duties
description: Gouge turns the glass around and speaks to children about the sacred duty of honoring parents — through inward reverence, outward obedience, and grateful care that extends into adulthood.
memoryVerse: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. -- Ephesians 6:1
discussionQuestions: What is the difference between obeying with a willing spirit and obeying with a resentful heart?
What does 'obey your parents in the Lord' mean? Can you think of situations where this distinction matters?
What does honoring your parents look like as an adult?

title: Speaking Life in the Home
subtitle: William Gouge — Domestical Duties
description: Discover Gouge's teaching on household speech — how the words we speak to one another shape the atmosphere of the home, and how kindness, tenderheartedness, and forgiveness transform family life.
memoryVerse: Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers. -- Ephesians 4:29
discussionQuestions: What does it feel like when someone speaks grace-filled words to you? Can you give an example?
Why do you think people are often kinder to strangers than to their own family?
What is one change each of us could make in the way we speak to one another this week?

title: The Household at Prayer
subtitle: William Gouge — Domestical Duties
description: Close the first week with Gouge's passionate call to family worship — Scripture reading, prayer, and singing — as the crown and summit of the Christian household.
memoryVerse: But as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. -- Joshua 24:15
discussionQuestions: What does it mean to make a family commitment to serve God, not just an individual one?
Which of the three elements of family worship does our family practice most? Which do we need to strengthen?
What are the biggest obstacles to regular family worship in our home?

title: The Power of a Godly Woman
subtitle: John Angell James — Female Piety
description: Meet John Angell James, beloved Victorian pastor, and explore his tribute to the incalculable influence of godly women — their inner beauty, their unique aptitude for piety, and their power to shape home and world.
memoryVerse: A woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised. -- Proverbs 31:30
discussionQuestions: What does meekness mean in the Bible? How is it different from weakness?
Can you name some women from the Gospels and describe their faith?
What godly women have had the greatest influence on our family?

title: The Godly Mother's Influence
subtitle: John Angell James — Female Piety
description: James reveals the extraordinary, generation-spanning influence of a godly mother — from Lois and Eunice to Monica and Augustine — showing that the most powerful sermons are often preached at the hearth.
memoryVerse: From a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. -- 2 Timothy 3:15
discussionQuestions: What are some of the earliest spiritual lessons you remember learning? Who taught them to you?
How does a parent teach without speaking — through example alone?
What does Monica's example teach us about persevering in prayer for our loved ones?

title: The Daughters of Sarah
subtitle: John Angell James — Female Piety
description: Explore the godly wife's power to influence her husband through chaste conduct, a meek spirit, and fearless faith — qualities that can win even an unbelieving spouse without a word.
memoryVerse: The ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. -- 1 Peter 3:4
discussionQuestions: How does a godly example speak louder than words?
What does it mean to 'not be afraid with any amazement'? How does trust in God produce fearlessness?
How does one person's attitude affect the atmosphere of the whole household?

title: Piety in the Daily Round
subtitle: John Angell James — Female Piety
description: James shows that true godliness fills the ordinary hours with sacred purpose — transforming mundane duties into acts of worship when done heartily, as to the Lord.
memoryVerse: And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men. -- Colossians 3:23
discussionQuestions: How does thinking of our daily chores as service to Christ change the way we approach them?
Can you think of someone whose quiet faithfulness has had a great impact?
What is one ordinary task we could begin to do more intentionally 'as to the Lord'?

title: The Woman of Influence
subtitle: John Angell James — Female Piety
description: James broadens the view to the godly woman's influence in church and community — from Dorcas's garments of mercy to the social reforms driven by faithful women of every age.
memoryVerse: This woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did. -- Acts 9:36
discussionQuestions: What does Dorcas's legacy tell us about the kind of legacy that matters most?
How do we keep our acts of kindness rooted in genuine love for Christ?
Is there a need in our community that our family could respond to together?

title: Guarding the Heart
subtitle: John Angell James — Female Piety
description: James warns against the subtle enemies of godliness — worldliness, complacency, harmful companions, and the neglect of the means of grace — and calls every believer to vigilant heart-keeping.
memoryVerse: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life. -- Proverbs 4:23
discussionQuestions: What are some ways a family can tell where their true treasure lies?
Have you ever experienced spiritual complacency? What helped you regain your hunger?
How does our family guard against worldliness, complacency, and neglecting the means of grace?

title: The Eternal Weight of Glory
subtitle: John Angell James — Female Piety
description: James lifts the curtain on eternity, reminding us that every prayer, every sacrifice, and every act of faithfulness in the home is preparation for an inheritance that will never fade.
memoryVerse: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory. -- 2 Corinthians 4:17
discussionQuestions: How can Paul call his sufferings 'light affliction'? What makes the comparison with glory so overwhelming?
What 'seen things' most distract our family from eternal priorities?
What would it look like for our family to live with eternity in view every day?

title: The Commentator's Household
subtitle: Matthew Henry — Family Worship and Bible Study
description: Meet Matthew Henry, the most beloved Bible commentator in the English language, and discover that his passion for Scripture began not in a study but at his father's family altar.
memoryVerse: O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day. -- Psalm 119:97
discussionQuestions: What practices in our home have helped us love Scripture?
Can we practice the three key questions — What does it say? What does it mean? How does it apply? — with tonight's Psalm?
How does prayer help us receive and apply what we read in the Bible?

title: A Church in the House
subtitle: Matthew Henry — Family Worship and Bible Study
description: Explore Henry's beloved treatise 'A Church in the House' and his practical, encouraging pattern for daily family worship that any household can follow.
memoryVerse: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them. -- Matthew 18:20
discussionQuestions: What does it mean for a home to function as a church?
Henry says God values sincerity over eloquence. How does this encourage our family?
What time of day works best for our family to worship together?

title: Searching the Scriptures Together
subtitle: Matthew Henry — Family Worship and Bible Study
description: Henry teaches us to read the Bible like the Bereans — with attention, questions, comparison, and prayer — transforming passive reading into active, life-changing engagement with God's Word.
memoryVerse: Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee. -- Psalm 119:11
discussionQuestions: What makes daily Bible reading so important? What happens when we neglect it?
Let us try Henry's method with tonight's passage: Who is speaking? What is the main point?
What is one passage of Scripture our family could memorize together this month?

title: The Secret Place of Prayer
subtitle: Matthew Henry — Family Worship and Bible Study
description: Henry leads us into the heart of family prayer — sincere, brief, inclusive, and faith-filled — showing how prayer teaches children that God is real, He listens, and He acts.
memoryVerse: The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much. -- James 5:16
discussionQuestions: If God knows what we need before we ask, why does He still want us to pray?
How could we involve every member of our family more fully in our prayer times?
Can anyone share a time when God clearly answered a prayer?

title: The Lord's Day in the Home
subtitle: Matthew Henry — Family Worship and Bible Study
description: Henry shows how the Christian Sabbath can become the crown jewel of the week — a day of joyful worship, restful renewal, and deepened family devotion.
memoryVerse: If thou call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord. -- Isaiah 58:13-14
discussionQuestions: What would it look like for our family to truly delight in the Lord's Day?
How could we begin the practice of discussing the Sunday sermon together?
How is the Lord's Day a gift rather than a burden?

title: Teaching the Catechism at Home
subtitle: Matthew Henry — Family Worship and Bible Study
description: Explore the Puritans' most powerful educational tool — the catechism — and Henry's practical method for using it to ground every family member in the fundamentals of the faith.
memoryVerse: Be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear. -- 1 Peter 3:15
discussionQuestions: What does 'Man's chief end is to glorify God and enjoy him for ever' mean in practical terms?
Why is clear thinking about God important? What happens when our understanding is vague?
Would our family be willing to try working through a catechism together?

title: The Legacy of a Faithful Home
subtitle: Matthew Henry — Family Worship and Bible Study
description: Close the week by tracing the golden chain of generational faithfulness from Philip Henry to Matthew Henry's immortal commentary — proof that a godly home produces fruit that endures for centuries.
memoryVerse: We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the Lord, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done. -- Psalm 78:4
discussionQuestions: What legacy do we hope our family's faith will leave behind?
What stories of God's faithfulness should our family be passing down?
What is one practice of family worship we want to make permanent?

title: The Pastor's Guide to the Home
subtitle: Richard Baxter — The Christian Directory
description: Meet Richard Baxter, the great pastor of Kidderminster, and discover his conviction that love, gratitude, and the virtues of Colossians 3 create the atmosphere in which a family can thrive.
memoryVerse: And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness. -- Colossians 3:14
discussionQuestions: What does a home governed by love look and feel like?
What is our family most grateful for right now?
Does the atmosphere of the home matter more than the activities performed in it?

title: Winning the Hearts of Children
subtitle: Richard Baxter — The Christian Directory
description: Baxter gives tender, searching counsel on how parents can win their children's hearts for Christ — through affection, patience, encouragement, and natural spiritual instruction.
memoryVerse: And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. -- Ephesians 6:4
discussionQuestions: Which dangers — severity, inconsistency, or hypocrisy — do we need to guard against most?
How is winning a child's heart different from merely commanding obedience?
What is one thing each family member could be encouraged about tonight?

title: Discipline That Heals
subtitle: Richard Baxter — The Christian Directory
description: Baxter offers the most balanced guide to parental discipline in Puritan literature — correction that flows from love, fits the offense, includes instruction, and always ends in reconciliation.
memoryVerse: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby. -- Hebrews 12:11
discussionQuestions: How does knowing that discipline comes from love change the way we receive it?
Why is restoring the relationship after correction so important?
Can you think of a time when correction helped you grow?

title: Redeeming the Time Together
subtitle: Richard Baxter — The Christian Directory
description: Baxter addresses the stewardship of time — identifying the great time-wasters (idle talk, excessive entertainment, procrastination) and commending a daily rhythm of worship, work, rest, and recreation.
memoryVerse: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil. -- Ephesians 5:15-16
discussionQuestions: Which time-waster is the biggest challenge for our family?
What would change if we truly believed our time together is limited and precious?
What is one practical change we could make to better redeem the time?

title: The Peacemaker's Home
subtitle: Richard Baxter — The Christian Directory
description: Baxter addresses family conflict with pastoral wisdom — showing that humility, quick reconciliation, honest communication, attentive listening, and free forgiveness produce a peace the world cannot give.
memoryVerse: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God. -- Matthew 5:9
discussionQuestions: How does humility — asking 'Could I be wrong?' — help resolve disagreements?
Why is it important to resolve conflicts quickly rather than letting them linger?
Is there any unresolved tension in our family that we could address tonight?

title: Preparing Children for the World
subtitle: Richard Baxter — The Christian Directory
description: Baxter addresses the bittersweet duty of equipping children for independent life — through spiritual formation, moral cultivation, intellectual training, and vocational guidance.
memoryVerse: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth. -- 3 John 1:4
discussionQuestions: Which dimension of preparation does our family emphasize most? Which needs more attention?
What is the difference between knowing about God and knowing God personally?
What do you most want your children to carry with them when they leave home?

title: The Eternal Perspective of the Home
subtitle: Richard Baxter — The Christian Directory
description: Baxter calls every family to view the home from the perspective of eternity — where the godly household is a foretaste of heaven and every act of faithfulness is an investment in imperishable glory.
memoryVerse: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad. -- 2 Corinthians 5:10
discussionQuestions: How does this eternal perspective change our family's priorities?
In what ways does our family's life together give us a glimpse of heaven?
If Christ were returning tomorrow, what would we do differently? What would stay the same?

title: Foundations of a Puritan Home
subtitle: Synthesis — Building a Puritan Home Today
description: Draw together the wisdom of all four teachers to identify the four pillars of the Puritan home — Scripture, prayer, character, and eternity — and build on the rock that will not be moved.
memoryVerse: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock. -- Matthew 7:24
discussionQuestions: Of the four pillars — Scripture, prayer, character, and eternity — which is strongest in our home?
Which teaching or author has had the greatest impact on our family this month?
What is one specific step our family can take this week to strengthen our foundation?

title: The Family Covenant
subtitle: Synthesis — Building a Puritan Home Today
description: Following the Puritan tradition of covenant-making, forge the wisdom of this month into a family covenant — a sacred pledge to live together under the authority of God's Word.
memoryVerse: And the people said unto the Lord, The Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey. -- Joshua 24:24
discussionQuestions: What would it mean for our family to make a commitment like Joshua's?
What are the most important commitments to include in a family covenant?
Would our family like to write a family covenant together tonight?

title: The Household of Faith
subtitle: Synthesis — Building a Puritan Home Today
description: Close the month with the great truth that undergirds everything: 'Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain.' Trust God with your family, walk in faithfulness, and watch Him build.
memoryVerse: Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it. -- Psalm 127:1
discussionQuestions: How does the truth that God builds the house change the way we approach family life?
What is the single most important lesson our family has learned this month?
What is one thing each family member wants to say to the others tonight?
